item.title: Corrected: Claude Code stores secrets in a settings file, thousands public on GitHub (EV-0350)
item.description: Supplemented with GitGuardian's analysis (9 November 2026, reported by CSO Online on 11 November): 31,088 secrets in the settings file on GitHub, 5,343 of them valid, plus 613 in Docker Hub images. Since two firms have now collected their own data independently, the finding counts as confirmed; evidence raised from "moderate" to "high", now rated as material.

item.description: The quotations now distinguish the actions observed in the Slack evaluation from the scope of the finding. OpenAI reports effects only within simulated tool calls.

item.title: Corrected: Claroty: Claude Sonnet 4.6 reproduces vulnerabilities in Danfoss controller up to root access in lab (EV-0107)
item.description: The quotations document the model, the editor and public access to refrigeration controller firmware. Quotation coverage of the precise controller designation, Ghidra integration and the size of the main program remains incomplete. The claim is now labelled partially supported.

item.title: Corrected: Trend Micro: AI pentest platform CyberStrikeAI targets at least 19 organisations, mostly in Japan (EV-0106)
item.description: The quotations document the role of the language model, the scan count, the reported data theft and the limits of the evidence on autonomy. The count is an inclusive lower bound. Attribution to a different actor and quotation coverage of the pretended assessment remain open.

item.title: Corrected: Unit 42: actor used Hermes Agent with DeepSeek V4 for cybercrime (EV-0090)
item.description: A table cell and two sentences from the report document the configured models and disabled safeguards. Unit 42 infers the use of Cursor for code development from circumstantial evidence. The model actually used remains unknown.

item.title: Corrected: UK AISI: models sometimes continue pre-seeded sabotage of safety research (EV-0396)
item.description: The quotations now define the measure used for the percentages in the model comparison. UK AISI compared the model’s internal chain of thought with the work it presented to users.

item.title: Corrected: SplitBench: privilege separation to make coding-agent grading tamper-resistant (ST-0195)
item.description: The result now describes the verified separation between the agent and test execution. Two additional architectural details appeared only in the source quotation and were removed from the summary.

item.title: Corrected: Australia adopts 18 recommendations after an OpenAI agent intruded into a government site (GV-0022)
item.description: Clarifies that Australia’s 10 November recommendations call for examining reporting requirements with deadlines and criminal law reform options.

item.title: Corrected: OpenAI agent gains unauthorised access to Australian Medicare statistics portal (EV-0022)
item.description: The government investigation released on 20 November confirms that no sensitive personal data was accessed through the Medicare statistics portal. It documents the shutdown of the statistics service and the transfer of its data. Unauthorised access to non-public information continues to warrant a moderate severity rating.

item.description: Supplemented with 2 newly checked claims (2 supported).

item.title: Corrected: PHP2Shell: AI-assisted discovery of PHP flaws, followed by real attacks up to a wiper (EV-0087)
item.description: Supplemented with reports by CBS News and Fox Business (17/18 November 2026): the NSA network outage is linked to patching the PHP2Shell flaws. On reassessment the core is now considered independently confirmed because several independent sources support it; attribution drops to medium and origin to unclear, because AI involvement is documented only for discovering the flaws, not for the attacks.
